actions: probe: one to three input sequences; analyze: reviewed arbitrary code over accumulated observations and history; submit: frozen predictor code and a research conclusion. Six exploratory rounds and at most one final submission round. Early submission allowed. No model call after submission execution.

arms.A: Current native research instructions plus common laboratory contract.
arms.B: Identical contract plus examples/research_comparison/experimental_design.md. No answers, mechanism names or a method menu.

budget_source: budget.json; $70 retained before first paid call within cumulative$5000; all previous20 unknown-cost requests retain coverage.
confirmation: Four input sequences frozen in simulator source before calls. They and their outputs are unavailable to research until the submitted predictor is frozen. Execute all submitted final programs only after every project has finished its research responses, to avoid operator feedback from revealed confirmation. No changes to submissions after source review.
design: Two hidden worlds, two research arms per world; world0 orderAB, world1 orderBA each round. Same initial observations, tools, model and limits. Different prompts create whole adaptive trajectories; no causal claim from a single pair per world.
experiment_contract: Each protocol supplies u at integer seconds, each0..1, length1..80. Output at time t is recorded just after u[t] is set, before the next one-second evolution. Every protocol starts from the same fresh initial preparation; a run may have unobserved internal state. Measurement noise independent Gaussian sigma0.015, repeated protocols have fresh noise. Common deterministic noise for matching protocol and replicate index across both arms and worlds.
failure_policy: Do not regenerate returned responses or modify authored code. Operational errors and unsupported actions remain in the denominator. Bound-source and CPU review required. Source checks are not a sandbox. Preserve full failures, source-review waits, API accounting and wall time.
initial_data: One thirteen-step constant input u=1 run. The two mechanisms have exactly equal noiseless and noisy initial observations; tested before calls. This is deliberately a controlled identifiability challenge.
original_goal_status: active; all six original open acceptance items remain open.
question: Can a researcher actively design experiments to distinguish initially observationally equivalent dynamic mechanisms and predict their responses to new interventions?
reasoning_review: Before scoring final predictions, preserve hypotheses with predicted contrasts. Manually trace actual matched interventions, whether results support the claimed revision, and overclaims. Also retrospectively report RMS difference between the two constructed worlds for the actual chosen protocols, normalized by known noise; this is evaluator-specific discrimination, not universal information gain. No hidden keyword scoring or model judge.
scope: Controlled synthetic system-identification capability study, not real chemistry, a new scientific discovery, or broad capability acceptance.
scoring: Primary: equal-weight mean RMSE on four frozen unseen input protocols, using noiseless reference outputs and each arm's full acquired observations. Report botharms, all protocol errors, failures, no-submission outcomes and frozen initial-data exposure-decay reference. RMSE<=0.10 is a predeclared local prediction milestone, not scientific convergence.
worlds: Evaluator knows the two constructed mechanisms and parameters; research model sees neither simulator, parameter values, alternative-world outputs nor confirmation data. Full truth is published after the study for audit.
